```{r echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, include=FALSE}
d <- knitcitations::read.bibtex("publications.bib")
```

```{r echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, include=FALSE}

# Blog posts declare the paper they are about with `doi:` in their front
# matter. Collect those so each publication can link to its plain-language
# post. A post without a doi field is simply not matched.

normalise_doi <- function(x) {
  x <- tolower(trimws(x))
  x <- sub("^<|>$", "", x)
  x <- sub("^https?://(dx\\.)?doi\\.org/", "", x)
  sub("^doi:", "", x)
}

post_files <- list.files("post", pattern = "\\.qmd$", recursive = TRUE, full.names = TRUE)

read_post <- function(path) {
  lines <- readLines(path, warn = FALSE)
  fence <- which(trimws(lines) == "---")
  if (length(fence) < 2) return(NULL)
  yaml_lines <- lines[(fence[1] + 1):(fence[2] - 1)]

  doi <- stringr::str_match(yaml_lines, "^doi:\\s*[\"']?([^\"'#]+)")[, 2]
  doi <- doi[!is.na(doi)]
  if (length(doi) == 0) return(NULL)

  title <- stringr::str_match(yaml_lines, "^title:\\s*[\"']?([^\"']+)")[, 2]
  title <- title[!is.na(title)]

  data.frame(
    doi   = normalise_doi(doi[1]),
    url   = sub("\\.qmd$", ".html", path),
    title = if (length(title)) trimws(title[1]) else "Read the summary",
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

post_map <- do.call(rbind, Filter(Negate(is.null), lapply(post_files, read_post)))
if (is.null(post_map)) post_map <- data.frame(doi = character(), url = character(), title = character())
```

```{r echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, results = "asis"}
q <- capture.output(print(d, .opts = list(sorting="ydnt", bib.style = "authoryear", max.names = 50, dashed = F, style = "html")))

index <- length(d)
current_year <- 9999
entry_doi <- NA_character_
for(i in seq_along(q)){
  to_print <- q[i]

  # year headings
  if(i < length(q)-1) if(stringr::str_detect(q[i+1], "\\(20[0-9][0-9]\\)\\.")){
    new_year <- stringr::str_extract(q[i+1], "[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]")
    if(new_year != current_year){
      current_year <- new_year
      cat("##", current_year, "\n\n")
    }
  }

  # numbering publications
  if(stringr::str_detect(to_print, "<p><cite>")){
    to_print <- stringr::str_replace(to_print, "<p><cite>", glue::glue("<p><cite>[{index}] "))
    index <- index - 1
    entry_doi <- NA_character_
  }

  # An entry spans several output lines, so pick the DOI up wherever it falls
  # and attach the blog-post link at the closing tag.
  if (is.na(entry_doi)) {
    found <- stringr::str_extract(to_print, "10\\.[0-9]{4,}/[^\"<[:space:]]+")
    if (!is.na(found)) entry_doi <- normalise_doi(sub("\\.$", "", found))
  }

  if (stringr::str_detect(to_print, "</cite>")) {
    hit <- if (!is.na(entry_doi)) which(post_map$doi == entry_doi) else integer(0)
    if (length(hit) == 1) {
      link <- glue::glue(' <a class="post-link" href="{post_map$url[hit]}">Plain-language summary</a>')
      to_print <- stringr::str_replace(to_print, "</cite>", paste0("</cite>", link))
    }
    entry_doi <- NA_character_
  }

  # outputting
  cat(to_print, "\n")
}
```
